investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the runner produced zero evidence and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState was entirely unmet. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules and are therefore ineligible regardless of resource availability. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, the scheduler cannot place any remote-agent pod, and preemption is also blocked (no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes). The eval runner timed out waiting for the pod to become schedulable, returned no evidence, and the check failed against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259).

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: both nodes have consumed their full allocation of peer-pod VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the two eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any live workloads running simultaneously, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.
QUATERNARY — Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a prior eval run consuming vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from being scheduled.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster

No evidence payloads (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were produced because the underlying VM pod never became schedulable, so the eval runner never reached the state-polling stage.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 carry this resource and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time; the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because the VM pod could not be scheduled, createAgent() in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) never completed, and the check timed out after ~144s without writing any required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream API to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The /api/generate/image/stream endpoint received this error, emitted a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, and produced no image URL, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI organization account associated with the API key used by the eval runner at /api/generate/image/stream has exhausted its credit balance. The OpenAI API returned HTTP error type "insufficient_quota" with code "credit_balance_exhausted", which the AURA image generation stream handler surfaced as a generation_error frame with GENERATION_FAILED. Because the generation never completed, no generation_completed frame was emitted and no image URL was produced, causing both contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false. This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.

Less likely: The workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a job step error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) before writing a new status.json, leaving the stale artifact in place.

investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream API to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The /api/generate/image/stream endpoint received this error, emitted a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, and produced no image URL, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the runner produced zero evidence and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState was entirely unmet. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules and are therefore ineligible regardless of resource availability. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, the scheduler cannot place any remote-agent pod, and preemption is also blocked (no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes). The eval runner timed out waiting for the pod to become schedulable, returned no evidence, and the check failed against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259).

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: both nodes have consumed their full allocation of peer-pod VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are present on those nodes.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only two nodes. If affinity labels were recently changed or nodes were re-labeled, the effective pool may have shrunk unexpectedly.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the two eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any live workloads running simultaneously, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.
QUATERNARY — Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a prior eval run consuming vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from being scheduled.

Less likely: A GitHub Actions scheduling delay or queue backlog caused the workflow to be skipped or significantly delayed beyond its normal cadence, resulting in the snapshot not being refreshed in time.

Least likely: A misconfiguration in the workflow schedule (e.g., cron expression changed or disabled) caused the workflow to stop running on its expected interval. This is a hypothesis only — no workflow configuration file is present in the supplied source discovery artifacts.
